ownerDecisionsRecorded.backend: existing authority database through compiler-owned adapters

cases.setup: A source action mutates an authority row and enqueues one delivery in the same transaction.
cases.expect: Neither mutation, change revision nor deliverable intent is visible.

cases.setup: Mutation and outbox intent commit together.
cases.fault: The process crashes before publishing an in-memory wakeup.
cases.expect: Restart discovers exactly one durable intent with its original ID and version.

cases.setup: The same source operation/revision is submitted twice after a retry or duplicate activation.
cases.expect: A uniqueness guard returns one logical intent ID and does not create a second payload.

cases.setup: Worker A claims a pending intent with fencing generation n.
cases.fault: A's lease expires before any possible-effect checkpoint and worker B reclaims it.
cases.expect: B receives a greater generation; A cannot later acknowledge or checkpoint state.

cases.setup: Worker A commits possible dispatch before its lease expires.
cases.fault: Worker B attempts a reclaim while A's provider outcome is absent.
cases.expect: The intent is outcome_unknown and no second provider dispatch occurs.

cases.setup: Two intents share ordering key K and a third uses key J.
cases.fault: K's earlier intent is retry_wait or outcome_unknown.
cases.expect: The later K intent cannot overtake; J may progress independently.

cases.setup: An earlier intent for ordering key K ends in succeeded, cancelled or failed with proven no effect.
cases.fault: A later intent for K is pending.
cases.expect: The terminal record releases K; a later intent may progress without rewriting the earlier history.

cases.setup: A provider may have accepted an intent, but the acknowledgement is lost.
cases.fault: Worker restarts and a new interval scan runs.
cases.expect: The same intent remains inspectable and blocked; no automatic retry or resend occurs.

cases.setup: A fixed UTC interval fires several times while the worker is down.
cases.fault: The scheduler resumes after the missed occurrences.
cases.expect: One pending scan is created for currently eligible rows, not one run per missed tick.

cases.setup: A singleton schedule is still running when another interval fires repeatedly.
cases.fault: More ticks arrive before the current activation finishes.
cases.expect: At most one pending follow-up is retained and repeated ticks do not grow an unbounded queue.

cases.setup: A scan has more than 500 eligible stable test rows.
cases.fault: The activation reaches its row bound and the process restarts.
cases.expect: A durable keyset continuation resumes without gaps or duplicate effects; each activation remains bounded.

cases.setup: An intent is pending or waiting for a known-no-effect retry.
cases.fault: A trusted cancellation request commits before claim or dispatch.
cases.expect: The intent becomes cancelled and no effect is invoked.

cases.setup: Possible dispatch is committed and an external operation is in flight.
cases.fault: Cancellation is requested before a receipt is available.
cases.expect: Cancellation is recorded as requested; success, known failure or outcome_unknown is preserved rather than asserting rollback.

cases.setup: An adapter proves a listed transient failure occurred before any effect.
cases.fault: The attempt fails within its bounded budget.
cases.expect: Only the same intent ID and immutable payload may retry after bounded jitter, while consuming one cumulative finite intent budget.

cases.setup: All bounded attempts fail with proven no-effect outcomes.
cases.fault: The retry count or elapsed budget is exhausted.
cases.expect: One terminal failed/dead-letter record contains safe failure class and attempt evidence; later scheduled activations cannot reset the exhausted budget.

cases.setup: An authorized operator has trustworthy evidence that resolves the exact prior intent.
cases.fault: The operator explicitly requests the supported replay path.
cases.expect: Replay retains ID, payload version and ordering key, consumes the remaining cumulative budget, and cannot reset an exhausted budget or resend unresolved outcome_unknown.

cases.setup: A worker encounters an intent whose payload version has no registered handler.
cases.fault: The worker is deployed with an older schema.
cases.expect: The intent is held with a safe diagnostic and is not decoded under a different version.

cases.setup: A fixed 15-minute interval crosses a local daylight-saving transition.
cases.expect: UTC occurrences remain 15 minutes apart; operation clock and scheduled_for remain distinct.

nonClaims: Cases are not executable or passing evidence.
At-least-once delivery does not guarantee exactly-once provider effects.
A lease expiration or timeout is not proof that an external effect did not occur.
The candidate does not freeze final source grammar, numeric lease values, retention period, or operator UI.
